command.clock_set.description: Host to agent: Set the realtime clock: to `sec` (seconds since 1970), or by `step` seconds from now. Exactly one of the two.

command.freeze.description: Host to agent: Arm the packet trigger (hydo_fc, the F= fault): read the packets the image's iptables rules put into netfilter queue `queue`, count those with TCP payload in direction `dir` that contain `pattern`, and at the n-th hold it, stop the process tree of `h` (SIGSTOP, then wait until every thread is stopped), report `froze`, and only then let the packet through. After dur_ms of guest time the tree is continued and `resumed` reported. Every other packet is accepted at once. n = 0 never fires (a trace in `log`).

dur_ms.description: How long the tree stays stopped, in ms of guest time.

id.description: The command's id; every command has a higher id than the one before.

log.description: Write a trace line per payload packet to this file (hydo_fc's log format).

n.description: Fire at the n-th counted packet.

netns.description: Bind the queue inside this network namespace (a path such as /tmp/hydo/ns/redis; the rules that feed the queue must be in that namespace too), then return to the agent's own namespace. Needs the feature `freeze-netns`.

own_port.description: Otherwise: a request when its source port is this port (the service's own port, the peer being the workload's client).

pattern.description: Count only packets whose payload contains these bytes (%xx escapes any byte).

port.description: Otherwise: a request when its destination port is this port.

sip.description: A packet is a request when its source address is this IPv4 address.

v.description: The protocol version of the line.

description: One line of the conversation between hydo's host and hydo-agent, the guest's first process. Host lines are canonical JSON followed by a newline on the serial input; agent lines are framed on the console as `HYDO-AG <len> <crc32> <json>`.
